title: RNA-Stable Isotope Probing
author: Roey Angel
materials: Prepare the following solutions: All glassware and plasticware must be clean and free of RNA and RNAse. Glassware can be baked at 180 °C for 04:00:00

Gradient buffer (0.1 M Tris-HCl, 0.1 M KCl, 1 mM EDTA) pH 8.0 : 15.76 g, Tris-HCl 7.455 g, KCl 0.37224 g, EDTA Dissolve the salts in RNase-free water and fill up to 1000 ml . Filter sterilise (0.1-0.2 μm). Autoclave. Trizma® hydrochloride / Tris-HCl Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #T5941 Potassium chloride (KCl) Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #P9333 (CAS: 7447-40-7) Ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid disodium salt dihydrate BioUltra 98.5-101.5% Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #E1644-100G Store at Room temperature

For every two gradients, mix the following in a 50 ml tube (assuming 6 ml Ultracrimp, PA centrifugation tubes): 9.696 ml, CsFTA 2.166 ml, Gradient Buffer Room temperature Adjust the volumes if using different-sized ultracentrifugation tubes. Cesium Trifluoroacetate Solution FUJIFILM Wako Pure Chemical Corporation Catalog #031-13681 (CAS: 21907-50-6) Thermo Scientific TUBE PA ULTRACRIMP 6ML PK/50 (Ultracentrifugation tubes, Thermo Fisher Scientific, 03945, https://www.fishersci.com/shop/products/tube-pa-ultracrimp-6ml-pk-50/03945 )

To each tube add 2 µL of GlycoBlue, 10 % (v/v) Na-Acetate ( 3 Molarity (M) ), and 250 % (v/v) of absolute ethanol. Assuming 500 µL fractions were collected and 30 µL were spent for determining the density, add 47 µL Na-acetate and 1175 µL, ethanol (absolute) . GlycoBlue™ coprecipitant Thermo Fisher Scientific Catalog #AM9515 3M Na-Acetate pH 5.5 Thermo Fisher Scientific Catalog #AM9740 GlycoBlue is particularly advantageous here because otherwise, the pellet is completely invisible.

For each fraction, prepare the following mixture in a PCR tube: 10 µL, template RNA 3 µL, random hexamers ( 50 micromolar (µM) diluted 20x in RNase-free water: 2.5 micromolar (µM) ) Random hexamers Thermo Scientific Catalog #N8080127

If preparing CsTFA solution from powder: Pour 17.2 ml, gradient buffer directly into a 50 g, CsTFA vial. Mix by hand at Room temperature and then allow for the residues to fully dissolve during several hours or overnight. If particle impurities are visible, filter the solution into a fresh bottle using a 0.1 or 0.2 μm filter. Store at 4 °C . 1. CsTFA will not dissolve well in pure water, and the pH will be too low 2. CsTFA powder is highly hygroscopic. It is, therefore, recommended to dissolve the entire content of the bottle immediately. 3. It is recommended to dissolve the powder first, using only around 16.5 mL of gradient buffer and adjust it afterwards. 4. Confirm that the density is 2 g ml -1 using an analytical scale and adjust the solution if necessary. Cesium trifluoroacetate Thermo Fisher Scientific Catalog #44633.18 (CAS: 21907-50-6)

steps.title: Prepare Ethanol Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare a 75% (v/v) molecular-grade ethanol solution using 75 ml of 75% ethanol and 25 ml of absolute ethanol with RNase-free water. Store at -20 °C.

steps.title: Calibrate Refractometer
steps.instruction: Calibrate the AR200 Automatic Digital Refractometer using 30 µL of RNase-free water at 20 °C. The device should read 1.3330 ± 0.0002 nD-TC.

steps.title: Adjust Gradient Mixture Density
steps.instruction: Measure the density of the mixture using a refractometer (30 µL sample) after inverting several times. Ensure the density is 1.3702 ± 0.0002 nD-TC; if not, correct by adding CsTFA or GB.

steps.title: Add HiDi Formamide
steps.instruction: Add 3.56% (v/v) HiDi (422 µL if volume was not corrected) to the mixture. It is recommended to add a slightly lower volume initially to avoid exceeding the refractive index.

steps.title: Verify Final Density
steps.instruction: Measure the density again to ensure it is 1.3725 ± 0.0002 nD-TC.

steps.title: Fill Centrifugation Tubes
steps.instruction: Transfer approximately 5.8 ml of the mixture into each centrifugation tube using a micropipette, filling only to the bottom of the neck.

steps.title: Add RNA Sample
steps.instruction: Add the RNA sample (preferably a highly concentrated solution to avoid diluting the gradient). Use 4 µL of RNA (150 ng/µl, total 75-600 ng), ensuring the amount does not exceed 100 ng per 1 ml of gradient mixture. For downstream PCR, 200-350 ng is sufficient.

steps.title: Balance Tubes
steps.instruction: Weigh each tube with caps. Ensure opposite pairs of tubes differ by no more than 0.1 g; adjust by adding gradient mix solution if necessary.

steps.title: Seal and Load Tubes
steps.instruction: Close the caps using a Thermo Scientific TOOL ULTRACRIMP EA or by hand. Place tubes in the rotor and screw the caps for the positions containing tubes using a torque wrench to approximately 120 in.-lb.

steps.title: Ultracentrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 130,000 x g (37,900 rpm for TV-1665 rotor) at 20 °C for 2 days and 17 hours using maximum acceleration and deceleration.

steps.title: Prepare Fraction Collection Setup
steps.instruction: Set up a fraction collection system using a precision pump and 2.0 ml low-binding collection tubes.

substeps.instruction: Fill a 20 ml syringe with RNase-free water and remove air bubbles.
Connect the syringe to a precision pump tube (approx 0.5 m) using a female Luer fitting on one end and a male Luer fitting on the other.
Attach a sterile 23G needle to the male Luer fitting end.
Mount the syringe on an NE-300 Just Infusion Syringe Pump.
Set the pump rate to 1 ml min-1 and collection steps to 00:00:30 (yielding 12 fractions for a 6 ml tube). Set volume to 'off' and diameter to '22 mm'.
Switch the pump on to purge air from the needle and tube, then switch off.

steps.title: Prepare Tube for Fractionation
steps.instruction: Remove the rotor and the first tube from the ultracentrifuge. Mount the tube upright on a stand with a clamp holder above the collection tubes.

substeps.instruction: Pierce the tube just below the neck using the 23G needle attached to the pump tube (avoid piercing through the other side; seal accidental holes with petroleum gel).
Use a sterile 26G needle to puncture a small hole at the bottom of the tube, then remove the needle.

steps.title: Collect Fractions
steps.instruction: Perform the fractionation by pumping water through the tube to push out the gradient.

substeps.instruction: Position the first collection tube directly below the bottom hole of the ultracentrifugation tube.
Start the pump and start a stopwatch as soon as the first drop falls.
Every 00:00:30 (or chosen interval), shift the rack to the next collection tube.
Continue until all fractions are collected, then close and label the tubes.

steps.title: Analyze Fraction Density
steps.instruction: Measure the density of 30 µL of each fraction using the refractometer, starting from the last (lightest) fraction. The gradient should range between 1.75 and 1.84 g ml-1 (for vertical rotors).

substeps.instruction: Convert refractive index (n) to density (ρ) using the formula: ρ = 31.495n - 41.439.

steps.title: Isolate RNA from Fractions
steps.instruction: Recover the RNA from the fractions through precipitation and washing.

substeps.instruction: Incubate fractions at -80 °C for 30 minutes.
Centrifuge at 14,000 rpm, 4 °C for 30 minutes.
Decant supernatant and wash once with 1 ml ice-cold 75% ethanol; invert several times.
Centrifuge at 14,000 rpm, 4 °C for 10 minutes.
Remove supernatant using a 1 ml tip, spin down remaining drops, and remove them with a 100 µl tip without disturbing the pellet.
Dry pellets for approximately 5 minutes at room temperature (under flame or laminar-flow hood) or under a filtered air stream.
Resuspend pellets in 10 µL RNase-free water or RNA Storage solution.

steps.title: First-Strand cDNA Synthesis
steps.instruction: Perform reverse transcription on the resuspended RNA pellets.

substeps.instruction: Incubate the mixture at 65 °C for 5 minutes in a thermocycler, then chill at 4 °C for at least 1 minute.

Prepare a master mix (multiplied by the number of fractions) and add 7 µL to each tube. Mix contains: 4 µL 5x Reaction buffer, 1 µL 10 mM dNTP mix, 1 µL 0.1 M DTT (optional), 0.2 µL RNase OUT (40 U/µl; optional), 0.2 µL BSA (20 µg/µl), 0.1 µL SuperScript IV RT (200 U/µl), and 0.5 µL RNase-free water.
Incubate in a thermocycler: 10 minutes at 23 °C, 60 minutes at 50 °C, and 10 minutes at 80 °C. Chill at 4 °C.

steps.title: qPCR Analysis and Data Plotting
steps.instruction: Quantify the isotopic enrichment using qPCR.

substeps.instruction: Dilute 1 µL of cDNA in 14 µL RNase-free water for qPCR (no dilution for standard PCR).
Evaluate enrichment using a qPCR assay (e.g., Bacterial SSU rRNA 338F-516P-805R).
Plot cDNA copy numbers against fraction density. Normalize results to the highest copy number or total copy numbers. Expect unlabelled RNA peak at ~1.78 g ml-1 and labelled RNA peak at ~1.82 g ml-1.
